patients.summary: Construction foreman with severe alcohol use disorder and compensated alcoholic cirrhosis who joined in 2021 with fatigue; workup found alcohol-related sideroblastic anemia and CLL. Over five years he has alcoholic and tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy with atrial fibrillation on warfarin, an atraumatic splenic rupture with splenectomy, a lung abscess, a Mallory-Weiss tear, aspiration pneumonia and a 2026 motor vehicle collision with massive transfusion, after which warfarin was stopped.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient. 54M, construction foreman, here because he is "run down." Partner pushed him to come. Several months of fatigue that has crept up on him; gets winded faster on job sites than he used to and needs to sit down during the afternoon. Denies black or bloody stools, hematemesis, nosebleeds. No chest pain, no fainting. Has not had a regular doctor in years.

Alcohol: drinks every day, 6 to 10 beers, has for about 25 years; on top of that several glasses of whiskey most days and heavier binges on weekends. Has had withdrawal seizures in the past (an admission in 2019) and was told then that his liver was cirrhotic. Hospitalized for pneumonia from aspiration twice (2018, 2020) at the hospital in town. Not interested in quitting today but willing to talk about cutting down.
Tobacco: former, 20 pack-years, quit about 5 yrs ago. No drugs.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: none.
FHx: father had alcohol use disorder and died with cirrhosis; paternal uncle had CLL; mother hypertension.

Exam: Thin-ish, no jaundice, no asterixis. Heart regular rate, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no tenderness, no fluid wave, liver edge not felt. No edema. Skin without bruising.

A/P
1. Fatigue, ? anemia - sending CBC with diff, iron studies, B12/folate, CMP. Will call.
2. Severe alcohol use disorder - AUDIT-C 11. Talked through risk to liver and seizure risk with any sudden stop; he should not stop cold on his own, call us first. Starting thiamine and folic acid.
3. Alcoholic cirrhosis by history - getting the 2019 records. Hep B/C and HIV screening today. Needs hep A/B vaccines if not immune.
4. Hx aspiration pneumonias, hx withdrawal seizures - noted.
5. HM: flu shot and PCV20 today. Colon screening next visit.
RTC 6 weeks.

documents.title: Lab Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 9.5 with MCV 68, but iron 210, ferritin 550, sat 88% - not iron deficiency, the opposite. WBC 10.8 with lymphs 60%. B12 and folate ok. AST > ALT, mild. Hep B/C and HIV negative, not immune to hep B. Microcytosis with iron loading in a heavy drinker - need marrow-level eval; referred to hematology. Message to pt.

documents.title: Your blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Piotr, your blood count is low (hemoglobin 9.5), which fits with how tired you've been. Your iron is actually high, not low, so iron pills are not the answer. I've sent a referral to hematology (blood specialists) to sort out why; their office will call you. Please keep taking the thiamine and folic acid. Hepatitis and HIV tests were negative. Call us if you notice any bleeding.

documents.title: RE: Your blood work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ok thanks. I work 6-3 so a later appt is better if they have it

documents.title: Prior Hospital Records (2018-2020)
documents.author: outside hospital
documents.body:
Records received from the county hospital, 38 pages, summary of relevant items:

03/2018 admission, 4 days: right lower lobe aspiration pneumonia after vomiting while intoxicated. IV antibiotics, discharged on oral course.

02/2019 admission, 3 days: generalized tonic-clonic seizure about 30 hours after his last drink; treated as alcohol withdrawal seizure, symptom-triggered benzodiazepines, no further seizures. CT abdomen done for abdominal pain on that admission: nodular liver contour consistent with cirrhosis. Told to stop drinking; no follow-up appointment kept.

11/2020 admission, 5 days: aspiration pneumonia, right lower lobe, after a binge. IV antibiotics. Discharged home.

Allergies on all admissions: NKDA.

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed prior hospital records. Confirms aspiration pneumonia x2 (2018, 2020), withdrawal seizure 2019, cirrhotic liver on 2019 CT. Problem list updated.

events.reason: Microcytic anemia, iron overload pattern, lymphocytosis

reports.text:
Specimens: peripheral blood smear; bone marrow aspirate, left posterior iliac crest, with iron stain; peripheral blood for flow cytometry.
Peripheral smear: dimorphic red cell population with a subset of hypochromic microcytes; scattered target cells. Leukocytes with an increased proportion of mature small lymphocytes with condensed chromatin; smudge cells present. Platelets adequate.
Bone marrow aspirate: adequate, cellular particles. Erythroid hyperplasia with mild dyserythropoiesis. Iron stain: increased storage iron; ringed sideroblasts 22% of erythroid precursors. Interstitial infiltrate of small mature lymphocytes. Myeloid maturation complete. Megakaryocytes adequate. No increase in blasts.
Flow cytometry (peripheral blood): monoclonal B-cell population, CD19+, CD5+, CD23+, dim CD20, kappa light chain restricted.
reports.conclusion: Ringed sideroblasts with increased iron stores, consistent with acquired sideroblastic anemia in the setting of alcohol use. Monoclonal B-cell population with CD5/CD23 coexpression, consistent with chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

documents.title: Hematology Consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Outside hematology/oncology clinic
Date of visit: 10/21/2021
Reason for referral: microcytic anemia with elevated iron indices; lymphocytosis

Thank you for sending Mr. Kirby, a 54-year-old construction foreman with heavy daily alcohol use and cirrhosis by history. He describes several months of fatigue and lower stamina at work. No bleeding, no fevers or drenching sweats, no weight loss, no lumps he has noticed.

Meds: thiamine, folic acid. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: no palpable cervical, axillary or inguinal adenopathy; no hepatosplenomegaly appreciated on exam; no petechiae.

Data: Hgb 9.5, MCV 68, ferritin 550, iron 210, TIBC 240. WBC 10.8 with 60% lymphocytes.

We reviewed the smear, performed a bone marrow aspirate with iron stain today, and sent peripheral flow cytometry (report enclosed). The marrow shows ringed sideroblasts with abundant storage iron, and flow shows a CD5+/CD23+ kappa-restricted B-cell clone.

Impression:
1. Acquired sideroblastic anemia, most likely from alcohol. This is the explanation for his anemia; it is not from marrow replacement by the CLL. It typically improves with abstinence. We are adding pyridoxine 100 mg daily; continue folic acid.
2. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia, early. No indication for treatment: no cytopenias attributable to CLL, no adenopathy, no symptoms. Observation with CBC every 3-6 months via PCP and clinic follow-up in about 6 months.

We strongly encouraged him to stop drinking. Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back after hematology. Marrow showed ringed sideroblasts - acquired sideroblastic anemia from alcohol - and flow cytometry shows early CLL, observation only. He took that in stride; his uncle had CLL. Started pyridoxine, taking it with the thiamine and folate most days.
Still drinking about the same. We talked about what a slow taper would look like; he says winter is slow at work and he might try then. Not interested in a program or meds for now.
Denies bleeding, fevers, sweats.
Exam: no jaundice. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abd soft, no ascites. No edema. No palpable nodes.
A/P
- Sideroblastic anemia: pyridoxine + folate per heme. CBC in a few months.
- CLL: heme following. Counts q3-6 mo.
- Cirrhosis: RUQ US for surveillance.
- AUD: counseled, follow up.
- HM: Tdap, hep A #1, hep B #1 today. FIT kit given.
RTC 3 months, nurse visit in a month for hep B #2.

reports.text:
Indication: cirrhosis, surveillance.
Liver: coarsened echotexture with a nodular surface contour. No focal hepatic mass. Main portal vein patent with normal hepatopetal flow.
Gallbladder: normal, no stones, no wall thickening.
Bile ducts: common duct 4 mm, no intrahepatic dilation.
Pancreatic head: unremarkable where seen.
Right kidney: normal size and echogenicity, no hydronephrosis.
No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Cirrhotic liver morphology without focal mass. No ascites. Patent portal vein.

documents.title: Imaging Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: RUQ US: cirrhotic liver, no mass, no ascites, portal vein patent. Repeat in 6-12 months. Pt notified via portal.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Community hospital ED, 01/02/2022
CC: short of breath
54 y/o M with heavy alcohol use and a recent anemia workup, 2 months of worsening breathlessness with exertion, now needs 3 pillows at night, legs swelling both sides. Drinks about six beers a day for 25 years, says no recent increase. No chest pain.
VS: BP 110/70, HR 96, RR 18, SpO2 95% RA.
Exam: JVP elevated, S3 present, swelling of both lower legs.
Labs: Na 138, K 4.2, Cr 1.1, BNP 900, AST/ALT mildly up, troponin negative.
CXR: cardiomegaly, congestion. ECG: sinus tach, nonspecific ST-T.
IV furosemide given. Admitted to medicine for new heart failure.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admit 01/02/2022 - discharge 01/05/2022
Diagnosis: new heart failure with reduced ejection fraction; alcoholic cardiomyopathy.
Course: IV diuresis with good urine output and improvement in orthopnea and edema. Echo 1/3: dilated LV, EF ~30%. Troponin negative. Monitored on withdrawal protocol, no significant withdrawal. Counseled at length to stop drinking as the likely cause and the main thing that could let the heart recover.
Discharge meds: furosemide 40 mg daily (new); thiamine 100 mg daily; folic acid 1 mg daily; pyridoxine 100 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week, cardiology referral.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 6 days after discharge for new heart failure, EF 30%, attributed to alcohol. Breathing much better, sleeping on one pillow. Swelling down. Taking furosemide in the mornings; doesn't like peeing at work.
Alcohol: says he has cut back to 3-4 beers. Hard to know.
Exam: weight down about 1.5 kg from Sept. JVP not elevated sitting up. Heart regular, no S3 heard today. Lungs clear. Trace ankle edema.
A/P
1. HFrEF / alcoholic cardiomyopathy: continue furosemide 40. BMP today. Referred to cardiology. Daily weights - gave him a log sheet. Low salt.
2. AUD: the heart is the strongest reason yet to stop; he heard it. Will keep at it.
3. Former smoker 20 pk-yr, quit ~5 yr: eligible for lung screening, LDCT ordered.
RTC 2 months.

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Hematology/oncology clinic, visit 04/07/2022
CLL, early, observation; acquired sideroblastic anemia, alcohol-related.
Interval: admitted in January with heart failure. Feels somewhat better. Still drinking daily, less than before by his report. Taking pyridoxine and folic acid "most days."
Exam: no adenopathy, no splenomegaly on exam.
Labs today: Hgb 10.8 (from 9.5), lymphocyte count stable.
Assessment: anemia improving. CLL stable without treatment indication.
Plan: continue pyridoxine and folate. CBC with PCP every 3-6 months. Return 1 year, sooner for new nodes, sweats, weight loss or falling counts.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group, visit 05/31/2022
Referred by PCP for heart failure with EF 30% (January 2022 admission).

He comes in for persistent symptoms. Over several months he has felt more and more worn out and has trouble getting through a normal workday. Walking a short distance he has to stop and rest. Every so often he wakes at night needing to sit up to catch his breath. His legs swell a little, worse by evening. Eating less, and down a few pounds without trying. No chest pain. No recent cough or infection.

Medications: was discharged on furosemide but stopped it within a month and has not been taking anything regularly. Vitamins on and off.
Alcohol: about 8-10 beers a day.
Allergies: NKDA.

BP 118/74, pulse 104 and irregular, SpO2 93% RA.
Tired-appearing man. JVP difficult to assess. Bibasilar crackles. Apical impulse displaced laterally. Irregularly irregular rhythm. Bilateral lower extremity edema.

ECG: atrial fibrillation, rate 104. CXR: cardiomegaly, pulmonary vascular congestion.

Assessment:
1. Atrial fibrillation, nonvalvular, new to us, with ventricular rates persistently around 100+. Not captured on his January ECG.
2. HFrEF, EF 30%. Alcohol is the leading cause, and ongoing uncontrolled rates likely contribute: tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy on top of alcoholic cardiomyopathy.

Plan:
- Rate control: metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily.
- Anticoagulation: warfarin 5 mg daily. INR goal 2-3; asked his PCP office to manage INR. Discussed bleeding risk, particularly with heavy drinking and falls.
- Furosemide 20 mg daily restarted.
- Abstinence is the single most important treatment.
- Return 3-4 months.

documents.title: Warfarin Start - INR Plan
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Cardiology letter received: AF, started warfarin 5 mg, metoprolol, furosemide 20. Our office to manage INR. Called pt: has picked up all three. Reviewed warfarin basics - same time each evening, no extra Tylenol over 2 g/day, tell us about any new antibiotics, and alcohol will throw the INR around. Watch for black stools, blood in urine, bad bruising. First INR Wed 6/8.

documents.title: Anticoagulation Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR 1.7 on day 8 of warfarin 5 mg. Still coming up, no change. Recheck at visit 6/16.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after cardiology. New dx of AF with rapid rates, on top of the alcohol cardiomyopathy. Started metoprolol, warfarin 5, furosemide 20. Taking them - partner set up a pill box. Feels less winded already; slept flat a couple nights.
Alcohol: still daily. Reviewed again that warfarin + binges + cirrhosis is a dangerous combination.
Exam: rhythm irregular, rate in the 80s. Lungs clear at bases today. 1+ ankle edema.
A/P
1. AF on warfarin: INR 2.3 today, goal 2-3. Continue 5 mg. INR q2wk then spread out.
2. HFrEF/cardiomyopathy: on metoprolol + furosemide 20. BMP today.
3. Sideroblastic anemia/CLL: heme saw him in April, Hgb up to 10.8.
4. HM: hep A #2, hep B #3, Shingrix #2 today.
RTC 3-4 months; INR in 2 weeks.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group, visit 09/22/2022
AF (nonvalvular), HFrEF EF 30%, alcoholic and tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy.
Feels better on metoprolol: walks the job site without stopping, no night breathlessness. Mild ankle swelling at day's end.
Meds: metoprolol succinate 25 mg, warfarin 5 mg (INR by PCP), furosemide 20 mg, thiamine, folic acid, pyridoxine.
BP 112/70, HR 78, rate controlled AF.
Lungs clear. No JVD. Trace edema.
Plan: continue current regimen. Again stressed abstinence. Follow up 6-12 months.
Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine f/u. Cardiology happy with rate control. Feels the best he has in a year; back to full days. Busy season at work.
Drinking: "less on weeknights," weekends still heavy. AUDIT-C 10. Not ready to commit to stopping.
No bleeding on warfarin. No black stools.
Exam: AF rate 70s. Lungs clear. Abd soft, no ascites. Trace edema. No asterixis.
A/P
- AF on warfarin: INR in range, continue 5 mg.
- HFrEF: euvolemic, continue metoprolol + furosemide.
- Cirrhosis: compensated. CMP today. US due next summer... actually due in 6 mo, will order spring.
- Sideroblastic anemia/CLL: CBC today.
- HM: flu and bivalent COVID today. FIT kit given.
RTC 3 months.

documents.body: Hgb 11.3, improving. Lymphs stable. LFTs at his usual mild AST>ALT, albumin and bili ok. INR 2.5.

documents.title: Anticoagulation Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. No change. Next 6 wks. Pt reminded about the FIT kit - still on his kitchen counter.
